items.q: A feeder supplies three motors with full-load currents of 20 A, 15 A and 10 A. The minimum feeder conductor ampacity is:
items.explain: 125% of the largest motor plus 100% of the others: 20 × 1.25 + 15 + 10 = 50 A.

items.q: A 25 hp, 460 V three-phase motor (Table FLC 34 A) requires branch-circuit copper conductors (75°C) of at least:
For the same 25 hp, 460 V motor (FLC 34 A), the maximum dual-element time-delay fuse for short-circuit and ground-fault protection is:
items.explain: Dual-element time-delay fuse: 175% × 34 = 59.5 A → 60 A standard size (next size up permitted by 430.52(C)(1) Exception 1).

items.q: A continuous-duty motor has a nameplate FLA of 32 A and a service factor of 1.15. The maximum overload relay setting is:
items.explain: 125% of nameplate for SF 1.15 or greater: 32 × 1.25 = 40 A. Use nameplate current, not the table value, for overloads.

items.q: A 45 kVA transformer (secondary 208Y/120 V, 125 A full load) is protected on both primary and secondary. The maximum secondary OCPD is:
items.explain: Secondary (9 A or more): 125% → 156 A; Note 1 permits the next higher standard rating, 175 A. With secondary protection in place the primary may be up to 250%.

items.q: A 75 kVA, 480 V three-phase transformer (primary current ≈ 90 A) is protected on the primary only. The maximum primary OCPD is:
items.explain: 125% × 90.2 = 112.8 A → next standard size 125 A (Note 1).

items.q: A motor has a table full-load current of 28 A. A non-horsepower-rated disconnect switch for it must have an ampere rating of at least:
items.explain: 115% × 28 = 32.2 A — so in practice a 35 A (or larger) switch, or a horsepower-rated switch of adequate rating.

items.q: Conductors supplying a capacitor bank must have an ampacity of at least what percentage of the capacitor's rated current?
items.explain: 135% of rated current, to allow for harmonic currents and capacitance tolerance.

items.q: An AC general-use snap switch may serve as the disconnecting means for a motor rated 2 hp or less and 300 V or less, provided the motor's full-load current does not exceed what percentage of the switch rating?
items.explain: 80% of the switch's ampere rating. (A general-use switch rated at least twice the motor FLC is the other common permission for stationary motors ≤ 2 hp.)

items.q: The branch-circuit short-circuit and ground-fault protective device for a hermetic refrigerant motor-compressor shall not exceed what percentage of the rated-load current (unless needed for starting)?
items.explain: 175% of RLA or branch-circuit selection current; may go to 225% where the compressor won't start otherwise. The nameplate 'maximum fuse/breaker' marking governs when present.

items.q: Per Table 430.248, the full-load current of a 2 hp, 230 V single-phase motor is:
items.explain: 230 V single-phase: 1 hp → 8 A, 1½ hp → 10 A, 2 hp → 12 A, 3 hp → 17 A, 5 hp → 28 A. Halve the 115 V values.

items.q: Table 430.52 gives a maximum of 250% for an inverse-time breaker. For a motor with 14 A FLC, 250% = 35 A, which is a standard size. If the calculation had produced a non-standard value, the Code permits:
choices: Rounding down to the next standard size only
Using the next higher standard size
items.explain: Exception 1 allows the next higher standard rating when the computed value doesn't correspond to a standard size. Exception 2 allows further increases (up to 400% for breakers ≤ 100 A) only when needed to start the motor.

items.q: Where a switch controls a lighting load from a box, the grounded (neutral) conductor generally must be:
choices: Provided at the switch location (with listed exceptions)
items.explain: Electronic switches and occupancy sensors need a neutral; 404.2(C) requires one at most switch locations, with exceptions where conductors can be added later (e.g., raceway with enough room).

items.q: Switches and circuit breakers used as switches shall be installed so the center of the grip of the operating handle, in its highest position, is not more than how high above the floor or working platform?
items.explain: 6 ft 7 in. (2.0 m), same as the OCPD rule in 240.24(A). Exceptions for busways, hookstick-operated switches, and equipment-adjacent switches.

items.q: A grounding-type receptacle replaces a non-grounding receptacle where no equipment grounding conductor exists in the box. Which is a permitted option?
choices: Install a grounding-type receptacle and bond its ground screw to the neutral
Install a GFCI receptacle marked 'No Equipment Ground'
items.explain: Options: another non-grounding receptacle; a GFCI-type receptacle marked 'No Equipment Ground'; or a grounding-type receptacle supplied through a GFCI, marked 'GFCI Protected' and 'No Equipment Ground'. Never bond to the neutral.

items.q: A 15 or 20 A, 125 V receptacle installed outdoors in a wet location requires:
choices: A weatherproof cover that is weatherproof only when closed
An enclosure that is weatherproof whether or not a plug is inserted (in-use cover), with a listed weather-resistant receptacle
No cover if under a roof overhang
items.explain: Wet locations: in-use (bubble) cover plus a weather-resistant (WR) receptacle. Damp locations may use a cover weatherproof when closed.

items.q: In dwelling units, 15 and 20 A, 125 and 250 V receptacles in the areas specified in 210.52 generally must be:
items.explain: Tamper-resistant receptacles are required in dwellings (and in guest rooms, child-care facilities, etc.) with exceptions for receptacles above 5½ ft, dedicated appliance receptacles, and a few others.

items.q: The circuit directory of a panelboard must:
choices: List only the main breaker size
Legibly identify every circuit and modification for its clear, evident, and specific purpose
items.explain: Identification must be specific enough to distinguish circuits — 'lights' isn't enough; location and purpose are. Spare positions get labeled too.

items.q: A panelboard shall be protected on its supply side by an overcurrent device having a rating:
choices: Not greater than that of the panelboard
Of at least 125% of the panelboard rating
Equal to the feeder conductor ampacity only
items.explain: The panelboard's rating is the ceiling for the supply OCPD, with exceptions for panelboards fed from a protected transformer secondary and for existing 'lighting and appliance' panels.

items.q: In a clothes closet, a surface-mounted incandescent or LED luminaire with a completely enclosed light source must have at least what clearance from the nearest point of the storage space?
items.explain: Surface-mounted incandescent/LED enclosed: 12 in. Surface fluorescent and recessed enclosed incandescent/LED/fluorescent: 6 in. Luminaires identified for storage areas may be inside the storage space.

items.q: Cord-connected, chain-hung, or pendant luminaires and ceiling-suspended fans shall not be located within what zone around a bathtub rim or shower threshold?
items.explain: The bathtub/shower zone is 3 ft horizontally and 8 ft vertically from the top of the rim or threshold.

items.q: For a permanently connected appliance rated over 300 VA, the branch-circuit switch or circuit breaker may serve as the disconnect if it is:
choices: Within sight of the appliance or capable of being locked in the open position
Located in the same panel as the service
items.explain: Within sight, or lockable with the locking provision remaining in place whether or not the lock is installed.

items.q: A cord-and-plug-connected kitchen waste disposer's cord must be between:
items.explain: Disposer: 18–36 in. Built-in dishwasher or trash compactor: 3 ft to 6½ ft measured from the plug face to the plane of the appliance's rear.

items.q: When sizing branch-circuit conductors and short-circuit/ground-fault protection for a motor, the full-load current is taken from:
items.explain: Use the NEC tables for conductors, OCPD and disconnects; use the nameplate current for sizing overload protection (430.6(A)(2)).

items.q: A 10 hp, 230 V, three-phase motor (table FLC 28 A) requires branch-circuit conductors with an ampacity of at least:
items.explain: Single motor: 125% of table FLC = 28 × 1.25 = 35 A.

items.q: For the same 10 hp, 230 V, 3-phase motor (FLC 28 A), the maximum rating of an inverse-time circuit breaker for short-circuit and ground-fault protection is:
items.explain: Inverse-time breaker: 250% × 28 = 70 A (a standard size). Nontime-delay fuse 300%, dual-element time-delay fuse 175%, instantaneous-trip breaker 800%.

items.q: A continuous-duty motor with a marked service factor of 1.15 requires a separate overload device set at no more than what percentage of the nameplate full-load current?
items.explain: 125% for service factor 1.15 or more, or temperature rise 40°C or less; 115% for all other motors.

items.q: A disconnecting means for a motor must generally be located:
choices: Within sight of the motor location and driven machinery
items.explain: Within sight (visible and not more than 50 ft). The controller disconnect can serve if it is in sight of the motor, or with lockable provisions under the exception.

items.q: A motor-circuit disconnecting means must have an ampere rating of at least what percentage of the motor's full-load current?
items.explain: 115% of the table FLC, or an hp-rated switch of adequate rating.

items.q: Per Table 430.248, the full-load current of a 1 hp, 115 V, single-phase motor is:
items.explain: 115 V single-phase: ½ hp 9.8 A, ¾ hp 13.8 A, 1 hp 16 A, 1½ hp 20 A, 2 hp 24 A. At 230 V the values halve.

items.q: Branch-circuit conductors for a single hermetic refrigerant motor-compressor must have an ampacity of at least what percentage of the rated-load current or branch-circuit selection current, whichever is greater?
items.explain: 125% — and the disconnect must be within sight and readily accessible (440.14).

items.q: A transformer rated 1000 V or less, protected on the primary side only, with a primary current of 9 A or more, requires a primary OCPD rated not more than:
items.explain: 125% of primary current (next standard size up permitted per Note 1). 2–9 A → 167%; less than 2 A → 300%.

items.q: A 1000 V-or-less transformer with primary-only protection has a primary current of 6 A. The maximum primary OCPD is:
items.explain: Primary currents from 2 to less than 9 A → 167%. Below 2 A → 300%.

items.q: A dry-type transformer rated 112½ kVA or less and 1000 V or less must generally have a separation of at least how much from combustible material (unless a barrier or complete enclosure is provided)?
items.explain: 12 in. (300 mm). Transformers over 112½ kVA need a transformer room of fire-resistant construction, with exceptions.

items.q: Per Table 430.250, the full-load current of a 5 hp, 208 V, three-phase motor is:
Receptacles installed in countertops or work surfaces:
choices: Shall not be installed in a face-up position unless listed for that purpose
items.explain: Face-up receptacles collect liquids and debris; only listed countertop assemblies are allowed.

items.q: Snap switches with metal faceplates shall be:
choices: Connected to an equipment grounding conductor (or protected by GFCI where no EGC exists)
items.explain: Metal yokes and faceplates must be effectively grounded; replacements without an EGC need GFCI protection or a nonmetallic, noncombustible faceplate.

items.q: A single non-motor-operated appliance is rated 20 A with no marked OCPD size. The branch-circuit overcurrent device shall not exceed:
items.explain: For appliances over 13.3 A with no marking, the OCPD can't exceed 150% of rated current: 20 × 1.5 = 30 A. Appliances rated 13.3 A or less: 20 A max.

items.q: Which installation is NOT covered by the NEC?
choices: A detached garage at a dwelling
Equipment under the exclusive control of an electric utility in its generating plant
A recreational vehicle park's site supply
items.explain: Art. 90.2(B) lists installations outside the Code's scope, including utility-controlled generation, transmission and distribution installations, ships, railway rolling stock, and mines.

items.q: Which NEC chapter is NOT subject to the requirements of Chapters 1 through 7 except where those chapters specifically reference it?
items.explain: Chapters 1–4 apply generally; 5, 6 and 7 supplement or modify them; Chapter 8 (communications) stands alone unless referenced; Chapter 9 holds tables.

items.q: Informational Notes in the NEC are:
choices: Explanatory material that is not enforceable
items.explain: 'Shall' marks mandatory rules, 'shall be permitted' marks permissive rules, and informational notes only explain.

items.q: Equipment that can be reached quickly without climbing over obstacles or using portable ladders is described as:
items.explain: 'Readily accessible' adds the 'quickly, no ladders or obstacles' condition to plain 'accessible'. Keys and tools for locks are allowed.

items.q: For equipment to be 'in sight from' another piece of equipment, it must be visible and not more than how far away?
items.explain: Visible and within 50 ft (15 m). This drives motor and HVAC disconnect placement.

items.q: A load is 'continuous' when the maximum current is expected to continue for:
items.explain: Three hours or more. Continuous loads are sized at 125% for conductors and overcurrent devices.

items.q: The maximum current a conductor can carry continuously under its conditions of use without exceeding its temperature rating is its:
items.explain: Ampacity depends on conditions of use — ambient temperature and number of conductors — not just the conductor's size.

items.q: For a circuit rated 100 A or less, conductor ampacity is generally selected from which temperature column unless the equipment terminations are marked otherwise?
items.explain: Terminations limit the conductor: 100 A or less (or 14–1 AWG) defaults to the 60°C column; over 100 A defaults to 75°C. Equipment marked 75°C allows the 75°C column.

items.q: A 480 V panelboard has exposed live parts on both sides of the working space (Condition 3). What minimum working-space depth is required?
items.explain: For 151–600 V to ground: Condition 1 = 3 ft, Condition 2 = 3½ ft, Condition 3 = 4 ft. For 0–150 V every condition is 3 ft.

items.q: The minimum width of working space in front of electrical equipment is:
choices: 24 in. or the width of the equipment, whichever is greater
30 in. or the width of the equipment, whichever is greater
The width of the equipment only
items.explain: 30 in. or equipment width, whichever is greater, and doors must open at least 90°. Height is 6½ ft or the equipment height.

items.q: Listed or labeled equipment shall be installed and used:
choices: In accordance with any instructions included in the listing or labeling
items.explain: Manufacturer's listing instructions are enforceable through 110.3(B).

items.q: Arc-flash hazard warning labels are required on switchboards, panelboards, and similar equipment likely to require work while energized in:
items.explain: Field or factory marking to warn qualified persons, required in other than dwelling units.

items.q: The circuit conductors between the final overcurrent device protecting the circuit and the outlet(s) are the:
items.explain: Feeders run between the service equipment (or other supply) and the final branch-circuit overcurrent device.

items.q: Indoors, the dedicated equipment space above a panelboard extends from the floor to what height?
choices: 6 ft above the equipment or to the structural ceiling, whichever is lower
To the structural ceiling in all cases
items.explain: No piping, ducts or foreign equipment in that zone; sprinkler protection is permitted above it.

items.q: Minimum headroom (height) of working space for equipment operating at 1000 V or less is generally:
choices: 6½ ft or the height of the equipment, whichever is greater
items.explain: 6½ ft (2.0 m) or the equipment height. Exceptions exist for existing dwelling-unit service equipment up to 200 A.

items.q: A 'qualified person' per Article 100 is one who has:
choices: Skills and knowledge of the electrical equipment and installations plus safety training to recognize and avoid the hazards
items.explain: The definition is about demonstrated skills, knowledge and safety training, not a specific credential.

items.q: Three 1/0 AWG THHN (0.1855 in² each) and one 2 AWG THHN (0.1158 in²) are installed in EMT. The minimum trade size is:
items.explain: Total area = 3 × 0.1855 + 0.1158 = 0.6723 in². Table 4 EMT at 40%: 1¼ in. = 0.598 in² (too small), 1½ in. = 0.814 in². Use 1½ in.

items.q: How many 8 AWG THHN conductors are permitted in ¾-in. EMT?
items.explain: Table C.1: 8 AWG THHN — ½ in. → 3, ¾ in. → 6, 1 in. → 9.

items.q: Twelve 10 AWG THHN current-carrying conductors share a raceway in a 40°C ambient. The adjusted and corrected ampacity of each is approximately:
items.explain: Start at the 90°C column: 40 A. 10–20 conductors → 50%; 36–40°C → 0.91. 40 × 0.50 × 0.91 ≈ 18.2 A — so a 20 A device is the practical maximum, below the 30 A small-conductor cap.

items.q: A box contains six 14 AWG circuit conductors, two internal cable clamps, one single-pole switch, and three 14 AWG equipment grounding conductors. Minimum box volume?
items.explain: 6 conductors + 1 (all clamps together) + 2 (device yoke) + 1 (all EGCs together) = 10 volumes × 2.00 in³ = 20 in³.

items.q: Three 12-2 NM cables (each with a ground) enter a box that holds a switch and a duplex receptacle, with no internal clamps. Minimum box volume?
items.explain: 6 circuit conductors + 1 (EGCs) + 2 (switch) + 2 (receptacle) = 11 volumes × 2.25 in³ = 24.75 in³.

items.q: Two 2-in. conduits enter a pull box on the same wall and the conductors leave through two 2-in. conduits on the same wall (a U-pull). The minimum distance to the opposite wall is:
items.explain: 6 × 2 in. (largest raceway) + 2 in. (the other raceway in the same row on that wall) = 14 in. The 6× rule also applies between each entry and exit of the same conductor group.

items.q: Direct-buried conductors emerging from grade must be protected by an enclosure or raceway extending from the minimum cover depth up to at least how far above finished grade?
items.explain: Protection runs from the required burial depth (or 18 in. below grade) to a point at least 8 ft above finished grade.

items.q: The 75°C ampacity of 4/0 AWG aluminum is:
Electrical metallic tubing shall NOT be used:
choices: Where subject to severe physical damage
In wet locations with listed fittings
items.explain: EMT is thin-wall. It is also not permitted for direct earth burial where subject to corrosion unless protected, or to support luminaires except as permitted.

items.q: Between pull points (boxes, conduit bodies), a run of rigid metal conduit or EMT shall contain not more than the equivalent of how many degrees of bends?
items.explain: Four quarter bends (360°) total, including offsets, between pull points.

items.q: The sum of the cross-sectional areas of all conductors in a metal wireway shall not exceed what percentage of its interior area?
items.explain: Wireways: 20% fill (and adjustment factors apply only above 30 current-carrying conductors, 376.22(B)).

items.q: Where raceways contain insulated conductors of what minimum size must a fitting or bushing with a smooth insulating surface protect the conductors where they enter an enclosure?
items.explain: 4 AWG and larger conductors need an insulating bushing or an identified fitting at raceway terminations, unless separated by substantial insulating material.

items.q: Rigid PVC conduit in trade sizes ½ in. through 1 in. must be supported at intervals not exceeding:
items.explain: Table 352.30: ½–1 in. → 3 ft; 1¼–2 in. → 5 ft; 2½–3 in. → 6 ft; 3½–5 in. → 7 ft; 6 in. → 8 ft. Also within 3 ft of each termination.

items.q: The minimum cover for direct-buried UF cable (general case, not under a building or slab) is:
items.explain: Direct-burial cables: 24 in. RMC/IMC: 6 in. Nonmetallic raceways without concrete: 18 in. Residential 120 V, 20 A GFCI-protected branch circuits: 12 in.

items.q: Minimum cover for rigid metal conduit (RMC) or IMC buried in earth is:
items.explain: 6 in. for RMC and IMC. Under a 4-in. slab with no vehicle traffic, cover can be reduced further per the table.

items.q: Minimum cover for rigid PVC conduit buried in earth without a concrete envelope is:
items.explain: 18 in. for nonmetallic raceways listed for direct burial without concrete encasement.

items.q: A cable run through bored holes in wood studs must have the edge of the hole at least how far from the nearest edge of the framing member, or be protected by a steel plate?
items.explain: 1¼ in.; otherwise a steel plate or bushing at least 1/16 in. thick is required.

items.q: At each outlet, junction, or switch point, at least how much free conductor must be left for splices or device connections?
items.explain: 6 in. measured from where the conductor emerges from the raceway or sheath, and extending at least 3 in. outside a box opening smaller than 8 in.

items.q: The ampacity of 3/0 AWG copper THWN (75°C column) is:
The ampacity of 6 AWG copper at 75°C is:
items.explain: Copper 75°C: 8 AWG → 50 A, 6 AWG → 65 A, 4 AWG → 85 A, 3 AWG → 100 A, 2 AWG → 115 A, 1 AWG → 130 A.

items.q: Eight current-carrying conductors are installed in one raceway. The ampacity adjustment factor is:
Nine 12 AWG THHN copper current-carrying conductors share one conduit at 30°C. What is the adjusted ampacity, and what is the largest OCPD generally permitted?
items.explain: Start at the 90°C column (30 A) × 70% = 21 A. The small-conductor rule still caps 12 AWG copper at a 20 A device.

items.q: The temperature correction factor for a 90°C-rated conductor in a 45°C ambient is:
items.explain: 90°C column: 36–40°C → 0.91; 41–45°C → 0.87; 46–50°C → 0.82. Always start from the conductor's own temperature column.

items.q: Conductors may generally be connected in parallel only in sizes:
items.explain: 1/0 AWG and larger, with each set matching in length, material, size, insulation and termination method.

items.q: Using the 83% rule for a one-family dwelling, the minimum copper conductor size for a 200 A service is:
items.explain: 200 A × 0.83 = 166 A → 2/0 Cu (175 A at 75°C). Table 310.12 lists 2/0 Cu or 4/0 Al for 200 A.

items.q: For box-fill calculations, each 12 AWG conductor is counted at:
items.explain: 14 AWG → 2.00; 12 AWG → 2.25; 10 AWG → 2.50; 8 AWG → 3.00; 6 AWG → 5.00 cubic inches.

items.q: A device box contains four 12 AWG circuit conductors, two 12 AWG equipment grounding conductors, one duplex receptacle, and no internal clamps. Minimum box volume?
items.explain: 4 conductors + 1 (all EGCs together) + 2 (device yoke) = 7 volumes × 2.25 in³ = 15.75 in³.

items.q: For a straight pull of 4 AWG or larger conductors, the length of the pull box shall be at least how many times the trade size of the largest raceway?
items.explain: Straight pulls: 8× the largest raceway. Angle/U pulls: 6× the largest plus the sum of other raceways in the same row on that wall.

items.q: A pull box has one 3-in. and two 2-in. conduits entering the same wall for an angle pull. The minimum distance from that wall to the opposite wall is:
items.explain: 6 × 3 in. = 18 in., plus the other raceways on that wall (2 + 2) = 22 in.

items.q: The maximum fill for a raceway containing more than two conductors is:
items.explain: One conductor → 53%; two → 31%; more than two → 40%.

items.q: A conduit nipple not over 24 in. long between boxes may be filled to:
items.explain: 60% fill for nipples 24 in. or less, and the ampacity adjustment factors of 310.15(C) do not apply to them.

items.q: EMT must be securely fastened within how far of each box or termination, and supported at intervals not exceeding how far?
items.explain: Within 3 ft of each termination and every 10 ft. RMC and IMC share the 3 ft / 10 ft baseline.

items.q: Flexible metal conduit must be secured within how far of each box and at intervals not exceeding:
items.explain: Within 12 in. of terminations and every 4½ ft. Unsecured lengths up to 3 ft (6 ft for luminaire whips) are allowed where flexibility is needed.

items.q: Type NM cable must be secured within how far of every box and supported at intervals not exceeding:
items.explain: Within 12 in. of boxes and every 4½ ft. Horizontal runs through framing holes count as supported.

items.q: Type NM cable with 90°C conductors: what ampacity column may be used for the final ampacity?
items.explain: The 90°C rating may be used for adjustment and correction, but the final ampacity cannot exceed the 60°C column (12 AWG NM → 20 A).

items.q: Expansion fittings are required for rigid PVC conduit where the expected length change due to temperature is at least:
items.explain: ¼ in. or more in a straight run between securely mounted items. Table 352.44 gives the expansion per 100 ft.

items.q: Generally, raceways shall NOT be used as a means of support for:
choices: Other raceways, cables, or nonelectrical equipment
items.explain: A raceway can't carry other raceways or cables unless identified for the purpose or used to support Class 2 circuit conductors to the equipment the raceway serves.

items.q: All conductors of the same circuit, including the grounded conductor and equipment grounding conductors, shall generally be:
choices: Run in separate raceways to reduce heating
Contained within the same raceway, cable, or trench
Run with no more than two per raceway
items.explain: Keeping all circuit conductors together prevents inductive heating of metal raceways and keeps the fault-return path low-impedance.

items.q: A residential 120 V, 20 A branch circuit with GFCI protection, in direct-burial UF cable, requires a minimum cover of:
items.explain: 12 in. for residential branch circuits rated 120 V or less, 20 A or less, with GFCI protection.

items.q: A cable run parallel to a framing member must be kept at least how far from the nearest edge of the member, or be protected?
items.explain: Same 1¼-in. setback as bored holes, to keep nails and screws out of the cable.

items.q: Flexible cords and cables shall NOT be used:
choices: As a substitute for the fixed wiring of a structure or run through walls, ceilings, or floors
items.explain: 400.12 lists prohibited uses: substituting for fixed wiring, through holes in walls/ceilings/floors, through doorways or windows, attached to building surfaces, concealed, etc.

items.q: How many 12 AWG THHN conductors are permitted in ¾-in. EMT?
items.explain: Annex C Table C.1 (EMT): ¾ in. → 22 × 14 AWG, 16 × 12 AWG, 10 × 10 AWG THHN. Use Tables 4 and 5 when conductor sizes are mixed.

items.q: How many 10 AWG THHN conductors are permitted in 1-in. EMT?
items.explain: Annex C Table C.1: 1-in. EMT holds 16 × 10 AWG THHN (26 × 12 AWG, 35 × 14 AWG).

items.q: Boxes and conduit bodies shall be installed so the wiring inside:
choices: Can be rendered accessible without removing any part of the building or digging
Can only be reached by the utility
items.explain: Accessible without damaging the building finish. Listed boxes in underground installations may be covered by gravel or light aggregate if their location is marked.

items.q: What is the 75°C ampacity of 250 kcmil copper?
Which conductor is generally NOT counted as a current-carrying conductor for ampacity adjustment?
choices: The neutral of a 2-wire 120 V circuit
An ungrounded conductor of a 3-phase circuit
The neutral of a 3-wire circuit supplying nonlinear loads
items.explain: EGCs never count (310.15(E)). A neutral carrying only unbalanced current of a balanced circuit is not counted (310.15(E)(1)), but a 2-wire circuit's neutral and a nonlinear-load neutral do count.

items.q: Rigid metal conduit must be secured within how far of each box, cabinet, or conduit body?
items.explain: Within 3 ft of terminations (5 ft where structural members don't allow 3 ft), and supported every 10 ft; longer spans are allowed for straight runs with threaded couplings per Table 344.30(B)(2).

items.q: A Class II hazardous (classified) location is one where the hazard is from:
items.explain: Class I = flammable gases/vapors/liquids; Class II = combustible dust; Class III = ignitable fibers and flyings.

items.q: A location where ignitable concentrations of flammable gases exist under normal operating conditions is:
items.explain: Division 1 = present under normal operation (or frequently due to maintenance/leakage). Division 2 = only under abnormal conditions, normally confined in closed systems.

items.q: In a Class I, Division 1 location, a conduit seal entering an enclosure containing arcing devices must be installed within how far of the enclosure?
items.explain: Within 18 in. (450 mm), with only explosionproof fittings between the seal and the enclosure.

items.q: In a major repair garage with no mechanical ventilation, the space up to what height above the floor is classified as Class I, Division 2?
items.explain: Where ventilation is not provided, the entire floor area up to 18 in. above the floor is Class I, Division 2. With mechanical ventilation of at least 4 air changes per hour (or 1 cfm/ft²), exhausted within 12 in. of the floor, the floor area may be unclassified. Pits without ventilation are Division 1.

items.q: Each patient bed location in a general care (Category 2) space must be supplied by at least:
choices: Two branch circuits: one from the critical branch and one from the normal system
Three branch circuits from the life-safety branch
items.explain: At least two branch circuits, one from the critical branch and one from the normal system (or two critical-branch circuits under conditions).

items.q: Minimum receptacle counts at patient bed locations are:
items.explain: General care (Category 2): at least 8 receptacles. Critical care (Category 1): at least 14. All must be hospital grade and marked.

items.q: General-purpose receptacles near a permanently installed pool must be located at least how far from the inside walls of the pool?
items.explain: Not less than 6 ft. Pump-motor receptacles: 6 to 10 ft, single, locking, grounding, GFCI. All 125 V, 15/20 A receptacles within 20 ft must be GFCI-protected.

items.q: The equipotential bonding grid around a permanently installed pool uses a solid copper conductor not smaller than:
items.explain: 8 AWG solid copper (insulated, covered or bare), bonding the perimeter surface, metallic parts, shell steel, and equipment.

items.q: A luminaire mounted in a pool wall must have the top of its lens at least how far below the normal water level?
items.explain: 18 in. (450 mm) below normal water level, unless listed and identified for use at lesser depths (never less than 4 in.).

items.q: The maximum current of a PV source circuit is calculated as:
choices: 100% of the sum of parallel-connected module short-circuit currents
125% of the sum of parallel-connected module short-circuit currents
items.explain: 125% of Isc for the source circuit (accounts for irradiance above STC). Conductors are then sized at 125% of that maximum current (690.8(B)) — the familiar 156% net.

items.q: Under the rapid shutdown rules, controlled conductors located outside the array boundary must be reduced to not more than how many volts within 30 seconds of initiation?
items.explain: Outside the array boundary (and more than 1 ft from it): 30 V within 30 seconds. Inside the boundary: 80 V within 30 seconds, or a listed PV hazard-control system.

items.q: The maximum PV system DC voltage for a series string is based on the rated open-circuit voltage corrected for:
items.explain: Voc rises as temperature falls, so the lowest expected ambient temperature (or manufacturer coefficients / Table 690.7(A)) governs maximum voltage.

items.q: An emergency system's power source must be available to the loads within how many seconds of normal supply failure?
items.explain: Emergency (Art. 700): 10 s. Legally required standby (Art. 701): 60 s. Optional standby (Art. 702): no time requirement.

items.q: A 200 A busbar panel with a 200 A main breaker will have a PV inverter breaker connected at the opposite end of the bus. Using the 120% rule, the largest inverter breaker permitted is:
items.explain: 120% × 200 A = 240 A total; 240 − 200 (main) = 40 A inverter OCPD, with the inverter breaker at the opposite end from the main and a warning label.

items.q: Each commercial building or occupancy accessible to pedestrians must have at least one outlet for a sign or outline lighting at each entrance, supplied by a branch circuit rated at least:
items.explain: A 20 A branch circuit that supplies no other load, within 50 ft of the entrance (2020 relaxed the exact location).

items.q: A legally required standby system must have its alternate source available within:
choices: Any time set by the AHJ
items.explain: 60 seconds for legally required standby; 10 seconds for emergency systems.

items.q: The receptacle for a permanently installed pool's pump motor, where located near the pool, must be:
choices: Within 3 ft of the pool for convenience
Between 6 ft and 10 ft from the inside walls, single, locking and grounding type, GFCI protected
items.explain: 6–10 ft, locking/grounding single receptacle, GFCI-protected.

items.q: The PV system disconnecting means must be:
choices: Readily accessible and marked 'PV SYSTEM DISCONNECT' (or equivalent)
items.explain: Readily accessible, permanently marked, and (where the line and load terminals may be energized in the open position) carrying a warning label.

items.q: In agricultural buildings, 15 and 20 A, 125 V receptacles installed in areas with an equipotential plane, outdoors, or in damp/wet locations require:
items.explain: 547.5(G): GFCI for 125 V, 15 and 20 A general-purpose receptacles in areas with an equipotential plane, outdoors, in damp or wet locations, and in dirt confinement areas for livestock. 2020 clarified it applies only to those 125 V 15/20 A receptacles; a dedicated-load receptacle is exempt when a GFCI-protected receptacle is within 3 ft.

items.q: A Class 2 circuit is best described as one that:
choices: Is power-limited by its listed Class 2 source so it poses an acceptable shock and fire risk
Must be installed in rigid metal conduit
items.explain: Class 2 (e.g., thermostat and doorbell circuits) is limited at the source. Class 2 conductors are kept separate from power conductors (725.136).

items.q: A 12 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 6 Ω and 12 Ω. The circuit is connected to 48 V. What is the total current?
items.explain: Parallel pair: (6 × 12) / 18 = 4 Ω. Total = 12 + 4 = 16 Ω. I = 48 / 16 = 3 A.

items.q: A 40 Ω heating element is connected across 120 V. How much power does it dissipate?
A 208 V three-phase feeder carries 50 A over 150 ft (one way) on 6 AWG copper (26,240 cmil). Using K = 12.9, the approximate voltage drop is:
A 240 V single-phase circuit carries 30 A for 200 ft (one way). To hold voltage drop to 3% (7.2 V) with K = 12.9, the minimum copper conductor is:
items.explain: Required CM = 2 × K × I × L / VD = 2 × 12.9 × 30 × 200 / 7.2 ≈ 21,500 cmil. 8 AWG (16,510) is too small; 6 AWG (26,240) is the first size that qualifies.

items.q: A 120 V single-phase circuit carries 20 A for 100 ft (one way) on 10 AWG aluminum (10,380 cmil). Using K = 21.2 for aluminum, the voltage drop is approximately:
items.explain: VD = 2 × 21.2 × 20 × 100 / 10,380 ≈ 8.2 V (about 6.8%). Aluminum's K is roughly 1.6 × copper's, which is why aluminum runs need larger sizes for the same drop.

items.q: A balanced 480 V three-phase load draws 40 A per line. What is its apparent power?
A 75 kVA three-phase transformer is fed at 480 V. What is its full-load primary line current?
A 45 kVA three-phase transformer has a 208Y/120 V secondary. Its full-load secondary line current is approximately:
A single-phase transformer steps 7,200 V down to 240 V. When the secondary delivers 100 A, the primary current is approximately:
items.explain: Turns ratio = 7,200 / 240 = 30:1. Current is inversely proportional: 100 / 30 ≈ 3.3 A. Check: 7,200 × 3.33 ≈ 240 × 100 = 24 kVA.

items.q: Adding capacitors in parallel with an inductive motor load will:
choices: Raise the power factor and reduce line current
items.explain: Capacitive VAR cancels inductive VAR, so apparent power (and line current) drops while true power stays the same.

items.q: A load draws 10 kVA and consumes 8 kW. What is its reactive power?
items.explain: VAR = √(kVA² − kW²) = √(100 − 64) = 6 kVAR. Power factor here is 0.8.

items.q: A 240 V RMS sine wave has an approximate peak-to-peak value of:
Chapter 9 Table 8 lists 10 AWG uncoated copper at about 1.2 Ω per 1,000 ft. The resistance of a 500 ft length is approximately:
items.explain: Resistance is proportional to length: 1.2 Ω × (500 / 1,000) = 0.6 Ω.

items.q: A 15 kW, 480 V three-phase resistive heater draws what line current?
A 5 hp motor operating at 83% efficiency runs fully loaded for 10 hours. Approximately how much energy does it consume?
Two resistors in series across 120 V draw 2 A. One resistor is 20 Ω. The other is:
A 10 Ω and a 30 Ω resistor are in parallel and the total current is 12 A. How much current flows through the 10 Ω resistor?
items.explain: Current divides inversely with resistance: I(10 Ω) = 12 × 30 / (10 + 30) = 9 A; the 30 Ω branch carries 3 A. Check: 9 × 10 = 3 × 30 = 90 V across both.

items.q: After a capacitor in a DC circuit is fully charged, it behaves like:
choices: A resistor equal to its reactance
items.explain: Once charged to the source voltage, no further current flows — an open circuit to DC. Capacitors pass changing (AC) current, block steady DC.

items.q: A balanced delta-connected load draws 52 A of line current. The current in each phase winding is approximately:
items.explain: Delta: I(phase) = I(line) / 1.732 = 52 / 1.732 ≈ 30 A.

items.q: On a 208Y/120 V 4-wire system with linear loads, phase A carries 30 A, phase B carries 30 A, and phase C carries 0 A. The neutral current is:
items.explain: In = √(A² + B² + C² − AB − BC − CA) = √(900 + 900 + 0 − 900 − 0 − 0) = √900 = 30 A. With two phases equally loaded, the neutral carries the same as one phase.

items.q: A 240 V circuit supplies a 4,800 W resistive load through conductors with a total round-trip resistance of 0.2 Ω. The voltage drop in the conductors is approximately:
items.explain: Load current ≈ 4,800 / 240 = 20 A. VD = I × R = 20 × 0.2 = 4 V. (Strictly the current is slightly higher after the drop, but 4 V is the exam answer.)

items.q: A 120 V circuit supplies a 10 Ω resistive load. What current flows?
A 240 V, single-phase resistive heater draws 20 A. What is its power?
A 1,200 W heating element is rated for 120 V. What is its resistance?
Resistors of 10 Ω, 20 Ω, and 30 Ω are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
items.explain: Series resistances add: 10 + 20 + 30 = 60 Ω.

items.q: Two 30 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
items.explain: Equal resistors in parallel: R / n = 30 / 2 = 15 Ω.

items.q: A 10 Ω and a 20 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
Resistors of 10 Ω, 20 Ω, and 30 Ω in series are connected across 120 V. What is the voltage across the 30 Ω resistor?
items.explain: Total R = 60 Ω, so I = 120 / 60 = 2 A. Voltage across 30 Ω = 2 × 30 = 60 V.

items.q: At any junction in a circuit, the sum of currents entering equals the sum of currents leaving. This is:
items.explain: Kirchhoff's current law: charge is conserved at a node. The voltage law says voltage drops around a closed loop sum to the source voltage.

items.q: A sine-wave voltage reads 120 V RMS on a meter. What is its approximate peak value?
A 60 Hz AC supply completes how many full cycles in one second?
items.explain: Hertz = cycles per second. 60 Hz = 60 cycles each second (120 alternations).

items.q: An AC circuit has 30 Ω of resistance and 40 Ω of inductive reactance in series. What is the impedance?
items.explain: Z = √(R² + X²) = √(900 + 1,600) = √2,500 = 50 Ω. Resistance and reactance add as vectors, not arithmetically.

items.q: A motor circuit uses 2,400 W of true power while drawing 3,000 VA of apparent power. What is the power factor?
A 240 V single-phase load draws 25 A. What is the apparent power?
A balanced three-phase, 208 V load draws 30 A per line at unity power factor. What is the power?
On a 480Y/277 V system, what is the relationship between 480 V and 277 V?
choices: 277 V is half of 480 V plus a safety margin
277 V is the delta phase voltage
items.explain: In a wye, line-to-line voltage = line-to-neutral × 1.732. 480 / 1.732 ≈ 277 V.

items.q: In a balanced delta-connected load, line current equals:
items.explain: Delta: line voltage = phase voltage, line current = √3 × phase current. Wye is the reverse.

items.q: A transformer steps 480 V down to 120 V. What is its turns ratio (primary:secondary)?
items.explain: Voltage ratio equals turns ratio: 480 / 120 = 4, so 4:1.

items.q: A 10 kVA single-phase transformer has a 240 V secondary. What is the full-load secondary current?
A 25 kVA three-phase transformer has a 208Y/120 V secondary. What is the full-load secondary line current?
One horsepower is equal to approximately how many watts?
items.explain: 1 hp = 746 W. A 5 hp output is about 3,730 W.

items.q: A 5 hp motor operates at 85% efficiency. What is its approximate input power?
items.explain: Output = 5 × 746 = 3,730 W. Input = output / efficiency = 3,730 / 0.85 ≈ 4,388 W.

items.q: A 120 V single-phase branch circuit runs 100 ft (one way) on 12 AWG copper (6,530 cmil) and carries 16 A. Using K = 12.9, what is the approximate voltage drop?
items.explain: VD = 2 × K × I × L / CM = 2 × 12.9 × 16 × 100 / 6,530 ≈ 6.3 V (about 5.3% — above the 3% branch-circuit recommendation).

items.q: The NEC informational note recommends limiting branch-circuit voltage drop to what percentage for reasonable efficiency of operation?
items.explain: Recommendation (not a requirement): 3% on the branch circuit and 5% total for feeder plus branch circuit.

items.q: If the length of a conductor is doubled (same material and size), its resistance:
items.explain: Resistance is directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area.

items.q: In a 120/240 V single-phase, 3-wire circuit, line A carries 20 A and line B carries 14 A. What does the neutral carry?
items.explain: On a single-phase 3-wire system the neutral carries the unbalance: 20 − 14 = 6 A.

items.q: In a perfectly balanced three-phase, 4-wire wye system supplying linear loads, the neutral current is:
items.explain: Balanced three-phase currents are 120° apart and cancel in the neutral. Nonlinear (harmonic) loads can change that.

items.q: If the frequency applied to an inductor increases, its inductive reactance:
items.explain: XL = 2πfL — reactance rises with frequency. Capacitive reactance does the opposite.

items.q: As frequency increases, the capacitive reactance of a capacitor:
items.explain: XC = 1 / (2πfC) — higher frequency, lower reactance.

items.q: A 1,500 W heater runs 8 hours a day for 30 days. At $0.15 per kWh, what does it cost?
As the temperature of a copper conductor rises, its resistance:
items.explain: Copper has a positive temperature coefficient. This is why ampacity tables carry temperature correction factors.

items.q: Three 60 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
items.explain: Equal resistors in parallel: 60 / 3 = 20 Ω.

items.q: A current of 5 A flows through an 8 Ω resistor. How much power is dissipated?
Two 20 Ω resistors in parallel are connected in series with a 10 Ω resistor across 120 V. What is the total current?
items.explain: Parallel pair = 10 Ω; total = 10 + 10 = 20 Ω; I = 120 / 20 = 6 A.

items.q: A wattmeter connected to an AC circuit measures:
items.explain: A wattmeter responds to voltage × current × power factor — true power. VA requires separate voltage and current readings.

items.q: A voltage is induced in a conductor when it:
choices: Cuts through magnetic lines of force
items.explain: Faraday's law of induction — the basis of generators and transformers. Relative motion (or changing flux) between conductor and field induces voltage.

items.q: A three-phase, 208 V load draws 50 A per line. What transformer kVA is needed (minimum, at full load)?
In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current:
choices: Is in phase with the voltage
items.explain: ELI the ICE man: in an inductor (L), voltage (E) leads current (I); in a capacitor (C), current leads voltage.

items.q: A 7.2 kW resistive heater operates at 240 V single-phase. What current does it draw?
The DC resistance of 1,000 ft of 12 AWG uncoated copper at 75°C is approximately:
items.explain: Chapter 9, Table 8 lists roughly 1.9–2.0 Ω per 1,000 ft for 12 AWG copper. Each three sizes smaller roughly doubles the resistance.

items.q: A motor delivers 10 hp while drawing 9 kW from the line. What is its efficiency?
In a wye-connected load, the line current is:
items.explain: Wye: line current = phase current; line voltage = √3 × phase voltage.

items.q: A 15 kVA single-phase load at 240 V draws what current?
A three-phase, 480 V feeder runs 250 ft on 1/0 AWG copper (105,600 cmil) at 100 A. Using K = 12.9, the approximate voltage drop is:
In a series circuit, which quantity is the same through every component?
items.explain: Only one path exists, so current is identical everywhere. Voltage divides across the components.

items.q: A 1,800 sq ft dwelling has two small-appliance circuits, one laundry circuit, a 12 kW range and a 5 kW dryer. Using the standard method, the total calculated load is approximately:
items.explain: Lighting 1,800 × 3 = 5,400 + 4,500 (SA + laundry) = 9,900 VA → 3,000 + 0.35 × 6,900 = 5,415 VA. Range 8,000 VA (Table 220.55 Col. C). Dryer 5,000 VA. Total 18,415 VA ÷ 240 V ≈ 77 A — so the 100 A minimum of 230.79(C) governs.

items.q: The demand load for one 15 kW household range is:
items.explain: Column C gives 8 kW for up to 12 kW. For each kW over 12, add 5%: 3 kW over → 15% → 8 × 1.15 = 9.2 kW.

items.q: A four-unit building has one 5 kW electric dryer per unit. The dryer demand load for the service is:
items.explain: Table 220.54 applies 100% for 1–4 dryers: 4 × 5 kW = 20 kW. Demand factors begin at 5 dryers (85%).

items.q: Under the dwelling optional method, central electric space heating (including a heat pump's supplemental heat) is included at what percentage of nameplate?
items.explain: 220.82(C): air conditioning 100%; central electric space heating 65%; fewer than four separately controlled heating units 65%; four or more separately controlled units 40%. Use only the largest of the heating/cooling options.

items.q: An office has 100 general-use receptacle outlets (180 VA each). Applying Table 220.44, the receptacle demand load is:
Using the 83% rule, the minimum copper conductor for a 150 A one-family dwelling service is:
items.explain: 150 × 0.83 = 124.5 A → 1 AWG Cu (130 A at 75°C). Table 310.12 lists 1 AWG Cu / 2/0 Al for 150 A.

items.q: A service has 3/0 AWG copper service-entrance conductors. The minimum copper grounding electrode conductor to a metal water pipe electrode is:
items.explain: Table 250.66: 2/0 or 3/0 copper → 4 AWG copper GEC. (The 6 AWG cap applies only to the portion that is the sole connection to a rod, pipe or plate.)

items.q: A 60 A branch circuit requires a copper equipment grounding conductor of at least:
items.explain: Table 250.122: 30, 40 and 60 A → 10 AWG copper. 100 A → 8 AWG.

items.q: A 20 A circuit's 12 AWG ungrounded conductors (6,530 cmil) are upsized to 8 AWG (16,510 cmil) for voltage drop. The equipment grounding conductor must be increased to at least:
items.explain: Ratio = 16,510 / 6,530 ≈ 2.53. Required EGC = 6,530 × 2.53 ≈ 16,500 cmil → 8 AWG. Wire-type EGCs are upsized in proportion to the circular-mil increase.

items.q: A 25-ft tap is made from a feeder protected at 400 A. The minimum copper tap conductor (75°C) is:
items.explain: Tap ampacity ≥ 1/3 × 400 = 133.3 A. 1 AWG (130 A) falls short; 1/0 AWG (150 A) is the first size that qualifies.

items.q: A branch circuit supplies 80 A of continuous lighting load. The equipment is rated for 75°C terminations. Minimum copper conductor size?
items.explain: 80 × 1.25 = 100 A minimum ampacity before adjustment → 3 AWG Cu at 75°C (100 A). OCPD likewise 100 A (210.20(A)).

items.q: A service's calculated neutral load is 300 A. Applying the neutral demand factor, the required neutral ampacity is:
items.explain: The portion of the unbalanced load over 200 A may be reduced 30%: 200 + 0.7 × 100 = 270 A. Not permitted for the nonlinear-load portion.

items.q: Under the 2020 Code, a kitchen island with 36 sq ft of countertop requires at least how many receptacle outlets?
items.explain: One receptacle for the first 9 sq ft, plus one for each additional 18 sq ft or fraction: 36 − 9 = 27 → 27 / 18 = 1.5 → 2 more. Total 3.

items.q: A dwelling bathroom receptacle must be located within how far of the outside edge of each basin?
items.explain: Within 3 ft of the outside edge of the basin, on a wall or partition adjacent to it, or on the side/face of the cabinet (not more than 12 in. below the countertop).

items.q: An attached garage with electric power requires at least one branch circuit that is:
choices: 20 A, 120 V, serving garage receptacles with no other outlets (readily accessible outdoor receptacles excepted)
Any rating, shared with the laundry
items.explain: A dedicated 120 V, 20 A circuit for garage receptacle outlets; it may also supply readily accessible outdoor receptacles.

items.q: Overhead service conductors (300 V or less) pass over a roof with a slope of at least 4 in 12. The minimum clearance above the roof may be reduced to:
items.explain: General rule is 8 ft above the roof; 3 ft is permitted for roofs sloped 4 in 12 or steeper when voltage does not exceed 300 V between conductors.

items.q: The system bonding jumper for a separately derived system (such as a transformer secondary) is sized according to:
choices: Table 250.102(C)(1) using the derived phase conductors
items.explain: Same table as the service main bonding jumper, based on the derived (secondary) ungrounded conductors. The SDS grounding electrode conductor is sized from Table 250.66.

items.q: A metal in-ground support structure (building steel) qualifies as a grounding electrode when it is in direct contact with the earth vertically for at least:
items.explain: 10 ft or more, with or without concrete encasement. Multiple structures bonded together count as one electrode.

items.q: At an existing building, a concrete-encased electrode is NOT required to be part of the grounding electrode system when:
choices: The building has a metal water pipe
Using it would require disturbing the concrete
A ground rod is driven instead
items.explain: The exception covers existing buildings where the rebar is not accessible without disturbing the concrete. New construction must use the Ufer when present.

items.q: A 100 A feeder carries the entire load of a one-family dwelling to its main panel. Using Table 310.12, the minimum copper feeder conductor is:
items.explain: The 83% table applies to the main power feeder as well as the service: 100 A → 4 AWG Cu (2 AWG Al).

items.q: A multifamily service supplies 12 ranges, each rated 12 kW. Using Column C, the range demand load is:
items.explain: Column C, 12 appliances → 27 kW. (Column C runs 8 kW for one range up to 15 kW + 1 kW per range above 30.)

items.q: A dwelling's standard-method calculated load is 18,415 VA at 240 V (≈ 77 A). The minimum service disconnect rating and the minimum copper service conductor (Table 310.12) are:
items.explain: 230.79(C) sets 100 A as the floor for a one-family dwelling regardless of the 77 A calculation; Table 310.12 gives 4 AWG Cu for 100 A.

items.q: In a dwelling-unit living room, wall receptacles must be placed so that no point measured horizontally along the floor line of any wall space is more than how far from a receptacle?
items.explain: The 6-ft rule — which produces the familiar 12-ft maximum spacing between receptacles. Wall spaces 2 ft or wider count.

items.q: For kitchen wall countertop spaces, receptacles must be installed so no point along the wall line is more than how far from a receptacle?
items.explain: 24 in. — so countertop receptacles are at most 4 ft apart. Any wall counter space 12 in. or wider needs one.

items.q: Which dwelling-unit receptacle location does NOT require GFCI protection under 210.8(A)?
items.explain: 210.8(A) lists bathrooms, garages, outdoors, crawl spaces, basements, kitchens (countertop-serving), within 6 ft of sinks, boathouses, near bathtubs/showers, and laundry areas. Ordinary living areas are not on the list.

items.q: In a dwelling, 125 V receptacles installed within what distance of the top inside edge of a sink bowl require GFCI protection?
items.explain: Within 6 ft of the sink, measured from the top inside edge of the bowl.

items.q: A dwelling unit kitchen requires a minimum of how many 20-ampere small-appliance branch circuits?
items.explain: At least two 20 A small-appliance circuits serving the kitchen, pantry, dining and similar areas' receptacles.

items.q: The dwelling-unit bathroom receptacle branch circuit must be rated at least:
items.explain: At least one 20 A circuit for bathroom receptacles, with no other outlets unless it serves a single bathroom.

items.q: Which dwelling-unit area is NOT listed as requiring AFCI protection for its 120 V, 15 and 20 A branch circuits?
items.explain: 210.12(A) covers kitchens, family/dining/living rooms, bedrooms, closets, hallways, laundry areas and similar. Bathrooms, garages and outdoors are not listed.

items.q: A branch circuit supplies 40 A of continuous load and no noncontinuous load. The overcurrent device must be rated at least:
items.explain: Continuous load × 125% = 50 A. Conductors (210.19(A)) follow the same 125% rule before adjustment.

items.q: A 20 A branch circuit supplies two or more receptacles. What receptacle ratings are permitted?
items.explain: 15 A circuit → 15 A receptacles only (not more than 15); 20 A circuit → 15 or 20 A; 30 A → 30 A; 40 A → 40 or 50 A; 50 A → 50 A.

items.q: On a branch circuit supplying two or more outlets, cord-and-plug-connected utilization equipment not fastened in place shall not exceed what percentage of the circuit rating?
items.explain: 80% of the branch-circuit ampere rating for portable cord-and-plug equipment.

items.q: A dwelling-unit hallway requires at least one receptacle outlet when it is at least how long?
items.explain: Hallways 10 ft or more in length, measured along the centerline without passing through a doorway.

items.q: One- and two-family dwellings need outdoor receptacles accessible at grade level at the front and back, installed not more than how high above grade?
items.explain: Not more than 6½ ft (2.0 m) above grade. Garage receptacles use 5½ ft.

items.q: In an attached dwelling garage, at least one receptacle is required in each vehicle bay, installed not more than how high above the floor?
items.explain: Not more than 5½ ft (1.7 m) above the floor, one per vehicle bay.

items.q: In a dwelling, at least one wall-switch-controlled lighting outlet is required in:
choices: Every habitable room, kitchen, and bathroom
items.explain: Every habitable room, kitchen and bathroom. In rooms other than kitchens and bathrooms, a switched receptacle can substitute.

items.q: The general lighting load for a dwelling unit is calculated at how many volt-amperes per square foot?
items.explain: 3 VA/ft² of floor area (not counting open porches, garages, or unused/unfinished spaces not adaptable for future use).

items.q: In a standard dwelling load calculation, each small-appliance circuit and the laundry circuit are each counted at:
items.explain: 1,500 VA each — so two small-appliance circuits plus laundry add 4,500 VA before demand factors.

items.q: A 2,000 sq ft dwelling has two small-appliance circuits and one laundry circuit. Using the standard method, what is the general lighting and receptacle demand load?
For a household electric clothes dryer, the load used in the calculation is:
choices: 5,000 W or the nameplate rating, whichever is larger
items.explain: 5,000 W or nameplate, whichever is larger. Demand factors in Table 220.54 apply for 5 or more dryers.

items.q: Using Table 220.55 Column C, the demand load for one household range rated 12 kW is:
items.explain: Column C allows 8 kW for one range rated not over 12 kW. Over 12 kW, add 5% per kW above 12.

items.q: In other than dwelling units, each general-use receptacle outlet is calculated at:
items.explain: 180 VA per yoke/strap (a 4-plex counts at 360 VA).

items.q: The service disconnecting means shall be installed at a readily accessible location:
choices: Either outside the building or inside nearest the point of entrance of the service conductors
In the same room as the meter
items.explain: Outside, or inside nearest the point of entrance of the service conductors — not in a bathroom (230.70(A)(2)).

items.q: The maximum number of service disconnecting means permitted for each service is:
items.explain: Up to six, and in the 2020 edition each must be in a separate enclosure or compartment (230.71(B)).

items.q: The service disconnecting means for a one-family dwelling must have a rating of not less than:
items.explain: 100 A, 3-wire minimum for a one-family dwelling. Other installations: 60 A general; 30 A for limited loads of a single branch circuit; 15 A for one 2-wire circuit.

items.q: Overhead service conductors (not over 300 V to ground) passing over a residential driveway must have a minimum vertical clearance of:
items.explain: 12 ft over residential property and driveways; 10 ft above finished grade at the service entrance (≤150 V to ground); 18 ft over public streets and parking areas subject to truck traffic.

items.q: Service conductors installed as open conductors or multiconductor cable without an overall jacket must have a clearance of at least how much from windows designed to be opened?
items.explain: 3 ft from windows, doors, porches, balconies, fire escapes. Conductors run above the top level of a window are exempt.

items.q: The maximum standard overcurrent device rating for 12 AWG copper conductors (absent a specific exception) is:
items.explain: Small-conductor rule: 14 AWG Cu → 15 A, 12 AWG Cu → 20 A, 10 AWG Cu → 30 A (12 AWG Al → 15 A, 10 AWG Al → 25 A).

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a standard ampere rating for fuses and inverse-time circuit breakers?
A feeder conductor has an adjusted ampacity of 65 A and does not supply a multioutlet receptacle circuit. The largest standard overcurrent device permitted is:
items.explain: Next-size-up rule: when ampacity doesn't match a standard rating and the device is 800 A or less, the next higher standard rating (70 A) is permitted.

items.q: Under the 25-ft feeder tap rule, the tap conductors must have an ampacity of at least:
choices: One-tenth of the feeder OCPD rating
One-third of the feeder OCPD rating
One-half of the feeder OCPD rating
items.explain: 25-ft tap: at least 1/3 of the feeder overcurrent device rating, terminating in a single OCPD, protected from damage. 10-ft tap has its own conditions.

items.q: Overcurrent devices shall be readily accessible and installed so the center of the operating handle, in its highest position, is not more than how far above the floor?
items.explain: 6 ft 7 in. (2.0 m), with exceptions such as busways and devices adjacent to the equipment they supply.

items.q: In dwelling units, overcurrent devices (other than supplementary protection) shall NOT be located in:
items.explain: Not in bathrooms of dwellings or guest rooms, and not in the vicinity of easily ignitable material such as clothes closets (240.24(D)).

items.q: The portion of a grounding electrode conductor that is the sole connection to a ground rod is not required to be larger than:
items.explain: Rod, pipe or plate electrodes: 6 AWG Cu max. Concrete-encased electrode: 4 AWG Cu max (250.66(B)). Ground ring: no larger than the ring conductor.

items.q: A single ground rod electrode must be supplemented by an additional electrode unless it has a resistance to earth of:
items.explain: 25 ohms or less, otherwise add a second electrode spaced at least 6 ft away (250.53(A)(3)).

items.q: When two ground rods are installed, they must be spaced at least how far apart?
items.explain: Not less than 6 ft (1.8 m) apart. Rods must be at least 8 ft long and driven their full length (250.52(A)(5), 250.53(G)).

items.q: A concrete-encased electrode (Ufer) requires at least how much electrically conductive steel reinforcing bar of ½-in. minimum diameter?
items.explain: At least 20 ft of ½-in. rebar, or 20 ft of bare 4 AWG copper, encased in at least 2 in. of concrete in direct contact with earth.

items.q: A 100 A circuit requires a copper equipment grounding conductor of at least what size?
On the load side of the service disconnecting means, the grounded (neutral) conductor:
choices: Must be bonded to every panel enclosure
Shall not be connected to equipment grounding conductors or enclosures
May be used as the equipment ground for ranges
Must be re-grounded at each subpanel
items.explain: The neutral-to-ground bond happens once, at the service. Downstream, neutrals and EGCs stay separate so no neutral current flows on metal parts.

items.q: A feeder supplies a detached garage from a dwelling. At the garage panel, the grounded conductor:
choices: Is bonded to the enclosure and grounding electrode
Is kept isolated from the EGC and enclosure; an EGC is run with the feeder
items.explain: Run an equipment grounding conductor with the feeder and keep the neutral isolated at the second building. A grounding electrode is still required there (250.32(A)).

items.q: The bonding jumper for a building's metal water piping system supplied by a service is sized according to:
choices: Table 250.122 based on the largest OCPD
Table 250.102(C)(1) based on the service conductors
items.explain: Sized from the service-entrance conductors using Table 250.102(C)(1), and in the 2020 edition it need not be larger than 3/0 copper or 250 kcmil aluminum. (The 2017 edition pointed to this table too; earlier editions used Table 250.66.)

items.q: Which raceway is recognized as an equipment grounding conductor without added conditions on length or fitting type?
items.explain: RMC, IMC and EMT are EGCs by themselves. FMC and LFMC qualify only with listed fittings, limited OCPD size and a 6-ft total length limit. Nonmetallic raceways never qualify.

items.q: An insulated equipment grounding conductor shall be identified by:
choices: Green, or green with one or more yellow stripes
items.explain: Green or green with yellow stripes, or bare. White/gray is reserved for the grounded conductor (200.6).

items.q: An insulated grounded (neutral) conductor 6 AWG or smaller shall be identified by:
choices: A continuous white or gray outer finish, or three continuous white or gray stripes
items.explain: White, gray, or three continuous white/gray stripes on other than green insulation.

items.q: An 8 AWG copper grounding electrode conductor run along a surface must be:
choices: Protected in rigid metal conduit, IMC, PVC, RTRC, EMT, or cable armor
items.explain: GECs smaller than 6 AWG need raceway or armor protection. 6 AWG may be exposed along the structure if not subject to physical damage; 4 AWG and larger may be exposed.

items.q: A service has 500 kcmil copper service-entrance conductors. The minimum copper main bonding jumper is:
items.explain: Table 250.102(C)(1): over 350 through 600 kcmil copper → 1/0 AWG copper. Above 1,100 kcmil, use 12½% of the largest phase conductor area.

items.q: Each multiwire branch circuit must be provided with a means to:
choices: Simultaneously disconnect all ungrounded conductors at the point where the circuit originates
items.explain: A multipole breaker or handle-tied single poles at the panel. Conductors of a multiwire circuit must also be grouped (210.4(D)).

items.q: A feeder supplies 60 A of continuous load and 40 A of noncontinuous load. Before any adjustment or correction, the minimum feeder conductor ampacity is:
items.explain: (60 × 1.25) + 40 = 75 + 40 = 115 A. The OCPD follows the same math (215.3).

items.q: Using the optional method for a dwelling unit, the general loads are taken at 100% for the first 10 kVA and at what percentage for the remainder?
items.explain: 100% of the first 10 kVA, 40% of the rest; then add the larger of the heating or cooling loads per 220.82(C).

items.q: Service conductors are considered 'outside' a building when installed:
choices: Inside a metal raceway anywhere in the building
Beneath at least 2 in. of concrete under the building
Within 10 ft of the exterior wall
items.explain: 230.6 lists: under 2 in. of concrete beneath the building, within the building in 2 in. of concrete/brick, in a vault, in conduit under 18 in. of earth under the building, etc.

items.q: If a metal underground water pipe, a concrete-encased electrode, and a ground rod are all present at a building, which must be bonded together to form the grounding electrode system?
choices: All electrodes present must be bonded together
items.explain: All grounding electrodes described in 250.52(A)(1) through (A)(7) that are present must be bonded together. Metal water pipe must also be supplemented (250.53(D)(2)).

items.q: The two small-appliance branch circuits in a dwelling kitchen may supply:
choices: Receptacles in the kitchen, pantry, breakfast room and dining room, plus refrigeration equipment
items.explain: Receptacle outlets in the kitchen and dining-type areas (including the refrigerator, which may also have its own 15 A+ circuit). No lighting or other outlets.

items.q: When ungrounded conductors are increased in size to compensate for voltage drop, the equipment grounding conductor:
choices: Must be increased proportionately by circular-mil area
Can be omitted if the raceway is metal
items.explain: Wire-type EGCs are upsized in proportion to the increase in the ungrounded conductors' circular-mil area.

items.q: Generally, a building or structure served by a feeder from another building shall be supplied by:
choices: Only one feeder or branch circuit
items.explain: One supply per building unless a 225.30 exception applies (special conditions, different voltages, capacity, etc.) — parallel to the one-service rule in 230.2.
